source.title: Red-teaming LLM unlearning: LUNAR's "forgotten" knowledge is still recoverable

page_placements.theme: Recovery by sampling or alternative decoding

record.file_problem: not stated; the full post text is present
record.tranche_reason: The post reports recovery attacks on LUNAR-unlearned knowledge and qualifies the robustness result to one model, one synthetic benchmark and a single edited layer.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own LUNAR attack results. It also mentions prior work on fine-tuning recovery, prompting attacks and LUNAR's resistance to quantization; those cited results are not rows. The layer scan is used to locate the attack direction, and the cosine similarity characterizes that direction, so neither is recorded as a recovery result. The pass@k curve in Figure 1 is described without additional numerical values beyond those recorded below.
record.test_reason: The post runs its own recovery attacks on LUNAR-unlearned Llama-2-7B on PISTOL. GRPO raised pass@1 from 0.05 to 0.60, oracle SVD ablation to 1.00, and a blind difference-in-means ablation to 0.45. These results bear directly on whether unlearning resists simple attacks (A), on fine-tuning recovery (B) and on recovery by internal edits (C).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author concludes that LUNAR's single-layer, near-rank-1 redirection can be bypassed by GRPO and undone by activation ablation, even blind, so the knowledge persists. The author recommends pass@k/leak@k evaluation and notes that distributed real-world knowledge or multi-layer edits may resist more.
record.recipe_differences: The post applies LUNAR to Llama-2-7B and tests GRPO and activation-intervention attacks; it does not reproduce LUNAR's unlearning training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The blind activation attack's reported result is for layer 22 and alpha 0.5. The post says higher and lower alpha settings produce poor-quality outputs; it gives no further numerical results for those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Before any attack, pass@16 on the forget set was ~30% against pass@1 of ~5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearned knowledge leaks under repeated stochastic sampling even when pass@1 is low.

record.problems: The post tests only Llama-2-7B and a synthetic, highly localized PISTOL forget set. It uses a ROUGE verifier for GRPO, which the author notes may require privileged information, and tests LUNAR at only one layer rather than a multi-layer configuration. Generation quality is discussed but not quantified.
record.rows_left_out: No other numerical recovery outcomes are reported. The pass@k trajectory in Figure 1 has no additional values stated in the text; the layer scan and cosine similarity are used to identify or characterize the attack direction, not to report knowledge recovery.

untested.parts: Retained general ability (no utility or retain-set numbers are given); chance level for pass@1; other unlearning methods, models and real-world datasets.
Supervised relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; label-based fine-tuning; the number of examples needed.
Other unlearning methods; multi-layer LUNAR configurations.
Not tested; quantization resistance is cited from the LUNAR paper only.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context attacks are not tested. Repeated sampling (pass@16) is reported but is not a prompt change.

missing.what: Recovery as a function of ablation strength (alpha sweep). The text gives only the ~45% value at alpha 0.5.
Pass@k trajectory across GRPO epochs. The figure only; no values are given in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-peer-reviewed LessWrong post: a single model, a synthetic dataset, no uncertainty estimates. The record's capability_check of 'y' is doubtful: generation quality is discussed but no retained-utility metric is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not establish the chance level for its pass@1 measure or quantify retained general ability after the attacks. It tests LUNAR on one model and dataset, not other unlearning methods.
The post does not test recovery using a small set of unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact training examples. Its GRPO attack uses a ROUGE verification signal.
Tests activation-direction ablation on LUNAR, but not other unlearning methods or multi-layer redirections.
No quantization attack is run in this post.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context-information attack is run. Repeated stochastic sampling is reported, but it is not a test of those prompt changes.
No newer counter-method is tested for resistance to the attacks.

source_check.notes: LessWrong post from a BlueDot sprint: one synthetic benchmark, single-layer LUNAR only, no controls, no uncertainty. capability=y rests only on the qualitative generation-quality panel (Fig 2c); no utility or retain-set numbers. GRPO pass@1 (0.60) exceeds the initial pass@16 (~0.30), and train/eval overlap is not stated. So the ROUGE reward may have taught some answers rather than only amplifying tail ones. R3's 0.60 is below the oracle's 1.00; no pre-unlearning pass@1 is given.

statements.correction: Either drop R3 from this statement or add it as its own item: LUNAR Llama-2-7B, PISTOL (synthetic legal contracts). GRPO on forget-set prompts with a ROUGE reward and no target labels, 5 epochs: pass@1 0.05 -> 0.60. The text does not give the training-set size or say whether train and eval prompts are separate.
statements.problem: The statement cites R3 as support for 'fine-tuning on part of the forget set restores privacy and copyright targets'. The post fine-tunes with GRPO and a ROUGE reward, supplies no target labels, and uses synthetic legal contracts (PISTOL), not privacy or copyright data. The statement says nothing about this study.

statements.correction: Blind attack: a norm scan of all 32 layers picked layer 22 (the LUNAR layer) without the original weights. Ablation at alpha 0.5 gave pass@1 0.45, cosine 0.988 to the oracle direction. Alphas around 0.5 recover about 45% with good quality; higher or lower alphas give garbage or realistic but wrong text (Fig 2c). No other layers' ablations are reported. Oracle: 1.00.
statements.problem: 'Its blind attack works only at alpha 0.5 and layer 22' implies other layers were tried and failed. The post found layer 22 blind, by a norm scan of all 32 layers, and reports ablation only at that layer. On alpha, it says alphas 'around 0.5' work.
